label: eq:relationsMetaHahn1
title: Definition
body_md:
The meta Hahn algebra, denoted $m\mathfrak{H}$, is the algebra generated by three generators $X,\ Z$, and $V$ subject to the relations:
\begin{align}   
    [Z,X]&=Z^2+Z,\label{eq:relationsMetaHahn1}\\
    [X,V]&= \{V,Z\}+V+\xi I,\label{eq:relationsMetaHahn2}\\
    [V,Z]&=2X+\eta I\label{eq:relationsMetaHahn3},
\end{align}
where $[A,B]=AB-BA$ denotes the commutator, $\{A,B\}=AB+BA$ the anticommutator and $\xi,\eta$ are central parameters.

label: rem:Duality
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Duality}
    The meta Hahn algebra is not stable under taking transpose, however the operators $Z^\top,V^\top,-X^\top$ satisfy relations \eqref{eq:relationsMetaHahn1}-\eqref{eq:relationsMetaHahn3} with parameters $\xi,-\eta$. Taking this fact into account, representations of the negative type are readily seen to be obtained from the positive type by transposition up to the change of  parameters $a_n\to a_{n+1}, \beta\to \beta+1, \alpha\to \alpha$.

label: eq:Recurrence for U
title: Proposition
body_md:
The rational functions $\mathcal{U}_n^\varepsilon(x;a,b,c)$
satisfy the following three term recurrence relation
\begin{multline}\label{eq:Recurrence for U}
    x\left(A_n\mathcal{U}_{n-1}^\varepsilon(x;a,b,c)+B_n\mathcal{U}_n^\varepsilon(x;a,b,c)+C_n\mathcal{U}_{n+1}^\varepsilon(x;a,b,c)\right)\\
    =\left(A'_n\mathcal{U}_{n-1}^\varepsilon(x;a,b,c)+B'_n\mathcal{U}_n^\varepsilon(x;a,b,c)+C'_n\mathcal{U}_{n+1}^\varepsilon(x;a,b,c)\right),
\end{multline}
where 
\begin{align*}
    A_n&= -\frac{n(1+2\varepsilon)(c-n-1)}{2(b+n)(2b+2n+1)},\\
    B_n&= \varepsilon-\frac{(n+1)(1+2\varepsilon)(c+n)}{2(b+n+1)}+\frac{n(1+2\varepsilon)(c+n-1)}{2(b+n)},\\
    C_n&= \frac{2b+n+1}{2(1+2\varepsilon)(c+n-1)(b+n+1)(2b+2n+1)},\\
    A'_n&= \frac{n(1+2\varepsilon)(c-n-1)}{2(2b+2n+1)},\\
    B'_n&=-(1+2\varepsilon)\frac{c}{2} +a,\\
    C'_n&= \frac{2b+n+1}{2(1+2\varepsilon)(c+n-1)(2b+2n+1)}.\\
\end{align*}

title: Remark
body_md: Notice that the polynomial $\mathcal{F}_n(x)$ is the dual of $\mathcal{U}_n^{-1}(x)$ in the sense that $n$ and $x$ are exchanged between the two functions. This remark is connected to the fact that the negative type representation can be understood as the dual of a representation of the positive type as mentioned in Remark \ref{rem:Duality}.

title: Remark
body_md: The threshold $m=\alpha-\frac12$ is not an artefact of the method. The functions $\Gamma(c_m\pm iy)$ have poles at $y=\mp i(c_m+j)$; these are off the contour for every $m$, but they pinch the origin and cross as $c_m$ changes sign, and the masses \eqref{eq:masses} are exactly the residues they leave behind. The mass points $x_{m,j}$ lie on the quadratic lattice attached to the eigenvalues $\mu(x)$, and each of them is a pole of $\mathcal{G}_m$, which is why the factorized form \eqref{eq:factorization-GW}, in which $\Theta_m$ is regular there, is the right one in which to state the general relation.
